sources.title: Beihai Park in Beijing: Worth Visiting?
sources.content:
Beihai Park in Beijing: Complete Guide

Overview
Beihai Park offers a tranquil escape from Beijing's bustling attractions. Though less famous than the Great Wall or Forbidden City, it provides "a refreshing escape from the hustle and bustle" with beautiful scenery and fewer crowds.

Main Attractions
The White Pagoda stands as the park's iconic structure. Climbing it takes about 30 minutes, with easier steps on the east side. From the top, visitors can see the lake, surrounding ancient buildings, and potentially glimpse the Forbidden City's corner towers.
Other notable sites include the Five-Dragon Pavilion and Nine-Dragon Wall, featuring distinctive architectural styles. The park illuminates these structures at night, creating a magical atmosphere.

Seasonal Activities
Spring: Lotus flowers bloom beautifully along the lake
Summer: Various boats available (electric, pedal, rowboats, traditional-style)
Autumn: Ginkgo trees turn bright yellow, creating peaceful scenery
Winter: The lake freezes from late December through February, offering ice skating, ice karting, and other activities

Visitor Information
Hours: Peak season (April 1-October 31): 6 AM-9 PM (entry until 8:30 PM). Off-season (November 1-March 31): 6:30 AM-8 PM (entry until 7:30 PM)
Tickets: 10 yuan peak season; 5 yuan off-season (combined tickets available)
Duration: Plan approximately one hour, though it pairs well with nearby attractions
Transportation: Take subway line 6 to Beihai North Station

Dining
Fangshan Restaurant, located north of the park, specializes in imperial cuisine with "classical" ambiance and staff in traditional cheongsams. Advance booking recommended, especially on holidays.

Comparison
The guide recommends visiting the Summer Palace if choosing between the two, as it's larger with more attractions, though both can be visited if time permits.

sources.title: How to visit Beihai Park Beijing (Tips, Photos & Map)
sources.content:
Beihai Park Beijing - Complete Visitor Guide

Overview
Beihai Park is described as "the oldest imperial garden as well as one of the largest in China." Often overshadowed by the nearby Forbidden City, this historic site deserves visitor attention.

Historical Background
The park was originally constructed in 1166 during the Jin Dynasty and underwent repairs and rebuilds through Yuan, Ming, and Qing periods. It opened to the public in 1925. The name literally translates to "north sea," reflecting imperial traditions of calling lakes "seas."

Location & Layout
Situated about 10 minutes northeast of the Forbidden City in central Beijing, the park features five main areas: Jade Island, East Shore, North Shore, Circular City, and Arboretum. The park has four entrance gates (south, west, east, and north).

Key Attractions
White Dagoba: An important city landmark atop Jade Island
Nine-Dragon Screen: Notable architectural feature
Wulongting (Five Dragon Hall): Historic structure
Stone maze and temples: Various pavilions throughout

Visiting Tips
Best Times: Mornings offer peaceful atmospheres with locals exercising. Winter transforms it into an ice rink; spring brings flowers; autumn provides scenic lake views.
Entry Points: Choose gates based on your itinerary—suggested routes connect to Forbidden City, Jingshan Park, or Shichahai area.
Dining: The famous Fangshan Restaurant serves imperial court cuisine on Qiongdao Island.

Transportation
Access via subway Line 6, buses 5, 13, 42, 101-129, or various numbered routes depending on gate selection.

sources.title: Beihai Park Beijing: Tickets, Attractions & Travel Guide
sources.content:
Beihai Park Beijing: Complete Guide

Overview
Beihai Park is one of China's oldest and most well-preserved imperial gardens located near the Forbidden City in central Beijing. This 680,000-square-meter site spans over 1,000 years of history.

Key Facts
Ticket Price: CNY 10
Hours: April-October 6:00-21:00; November-March 6:30-20:00
Location: No. 1 Wenjin Street, Xicheng District
Visit Duration: 2-4 hours recommended

History
The park originated during the Liao Dynasty and was shaped by subsequent rulers including Jin, Yuan, Ming, and Qing dynasties. It reflects the ancient Chinese myth of three magical islands believed to grant immortality. Emperor Qianlong's renovations (1736-1795) established its current layout. The park opened to the public in 1925.

Main Attractions
White Dagoba: A 35.9-meter Tibetan-style stupa built in 1651, housing Buddhist relics and offering panoramic park views.
Nine-Dragon Screen: A 27-meter glazed-tile masterpiece from 1756 featuring 635 dragons total, representing one of China's three most famous dragon walls.
Quiet Heart Studio: An elegant Ming Dynasty garden-within-a-garden featuring pavilions, ponds, and rockeries.
Yong'an Bridge: A three-arched stone bridge rebuilt in 1743 with 48 carved balusters.
Five-Dragon Pavilion: Five interconnected Ming Dynasty pavilions forming an S-shape along the northwest shore.
Little Western Heaven: A Qing Dynasty complex built for the emperor's mother featuring the Hall of Pure Pleasure.

sources.title: Explore the Best Parks in Beijing - Jingshan Park And Beihai Park
sources.content:
Beihai Park - Complete Text Content

Location & History
Beihai Park, also known as Northern Sea Park, is situated just a stone's throw away from the north gate of the Forbidden City in Beijing's heart. It ranks among China's oldest and best-preserved imperial gardens, showcasing over 1000 years of history.

Design & Layout
Harmoniously blends the elegance of Southern Chinese gardens, the majesty of northern parks, and religious and imperial structures. The park spans 68 hectares, with Beihai Lake accounting for more than half of the park's expanse.

Imperial Legacy
The park served as a royal palace across the Liao, Jin, Yuan, Ming, and Qing dynasties. Much of today's architecture reflects Emperor Qianlong's vision during the Qing Dynasty (1644-1911 A.D.).

Architecture & Features
Visitors encounter a labyrinth of pavilions, halls, covered corridors, and temples, a delightful journey through architectural grandeur. The White Dagoba Hill provides spectacular panoramic views.

Panoramic Views
From atop White Dagoba Hill, visitors behold the crimson walls and golden tiles of Jingshan Park and the Forbidden City. The eastern view features five pavilions and Round City structures, with Zhongnanhai to the south.

Practical Information
Access: Take Subway Line 6, exit at Beihai Bei Station, Gate B entrance
Hours: Daily 6:30 am - 9:00 pm
Admission: 10 RMB (April-October); 5 RMB (November-March)

sources.title: Beihai Park - Beijing Government Official Guide
sources.content:
Beihai Park - Beijing Government Official Guide

Beihai Park is currently the earliest and best preserved classical imperial garden with the most profound culture in China. Located northwest of the Forbidden City, it is one of Beijing's oldest and most charming imperial gardens.

Admission & Hours
Peak Season (April 1 to October 31): 8:00-18:00 for scenic spots (admission 10 RMB). Off Season (November 1 to March 31): 8:30-17:00 (admission 5 RMB). Combined ticket: 20 RMB peak / 15 RMB off-season.

Foreign visitors need to call (010) 64037972 to make a reservation at least one day in advance.

Key Attractions
The White Dagoba stands at over 30 meters on Qinghua Island and is a symbol of both Beihai Park and Beijing City. The Nine-Dragon Wall, built during the Ming Dynasty, is the only double-sided one among the three existing ancient Nine-Dragon Walls in China.

Transportation
Subway line 6 to Beihai Bei (North) Station, Exit B. Bus routes: 13, 42, 90, 107, 111, 118, 609, 612, 623, 701 to North Gate.

sources.title: 北海公园 - 百度百科
sources.content:
北海公园综合信息

基本信息
北海公园位于北京市西城区，是国家AAAA级旅游景区。占地68公顷，其中水面积38.9万平方米，陆地面积29.3万平方米。这是中国现存历史上建园最早、保存最完整、文化沉积最深厚的古典皇家园林。

历史沿革概览
辽代：早在938年建都燕京时，城东北郊有湖泊名为"金海"，岛屿称"瑶屿"，是北海前身。
金朝：扩建瑶屿，金世宗仿北宋汴梁艮岳园，在中都东北郊以瑶屿为中心修建大宁离宫，"金海"改称"西华潭"，岛称"琼华岛"。
元朝：忽必烈三次扩建琼华岛，以琼华岛为中心在湖东西两岸营建宫殿，发展成"颇有气派的皇宫御园"。
明朝：永乐十八年（1420年）正式迁都北京，北海成为皇宫后花园。宣德年间进行大规模扩建修缮。
清朝：乾隆时期对北海进行大规模修葺增建，建起许多亭台楼阁。北岸的静心斋、东岸的画舫斋等"园中之园"成形。1900年八国联军侵华时遭严重破坏。
民国：1915年辟为公园，1925年正式对外开放，定名"北海公园"。
建国后：1979年后重新对公众开放，1987年被评为"北京新十六景之一"。

地理与气候
属大陆性季风气候，年平均气温10-12摄氏度，年降水量644毫米。北海是北京城内最大湖泊，水源以密云水库补给为主。

主要景点
琼岛景区：永安桥（三曲折三孔拱券石桥，莲花形望柱）、永安寺（1651年始建的白塔寺）、琼岛春阴碑（乾隆十六年立）、阅古楼（保存《三希堂法帖》石刻）、铜仙承露盘（仿汉武帝故事）、智珠殿（般若香台）
东岸景区：濠濮间、画舫斋、先蚕坛
北岸景区：小西天（极乐世界，最大方亭式宫殿建筑）、铁影壁（元代遗物）、九龙壁（双面七色琉璃壁，乾隆二十一年建）、静心斋（园中之园精品）、快雪堂书法博物馆、五龙亭、西天梵境
团城景区：承光殿（白玉佛，经八国联军洗劫）、玉瓮（至元二年制，重约3500公斤）

生物多样性
植物：桧柏、侧柏、白皮松、油松、国槐等，古树584株，乔木约5000株，灌木8000株。荷花品种丰富。
动物：花脸鸭、秋沙鸭、野鸭、鸳鸯等濒危物种。

文化活动
祈福文化盛典（自乾隆时期传承）、北海菊展（自1954年起，已办43届）、《印·静心》文化体验活动、冬季传统滑冰、安塞腰鼓表演

旅游信息
门票：旺季10元，联票20元；淡季5元，联票15元
开放时间：旺季（4-10月）6:00-21:00，20:30停止入园；淡季（11-3月）6:30-20:00，19:30停止入园
交通：公交3、13、42、701、107、111、118、101、103、109、124路；地铁6号线北海北站

保护与荣誉
1961年入选第一批全国重点文物保护单位，2024年北京中轴线被列入世界遗产名录。荣获北京"精品公园"等多项荣誉。

sources.title: Beihai Park, Beijing - Facts, History, Top Attractions, Tips
sources.content:
Beihai Park, Beijing - Facts, History, Top Attractions, Tips

Beihai Park is one of the oldest, largest, and best-preserved ancient imperial gardens in China with a history of more than 1,000 years. The park covers an area of 68.2 hectares with the water area accounting for more than half.

The park is designed based on the ancient Chinese myth of 'one pool and three fairy mountains.' The three fairy mountains are Penglai, Yingzhou, and Fangzhang, believed to be inhabited by immortals.

Foreign visitors need to call (010) 64037972 to make a reservation at least one day in advance during office hours from 9:00 to 16:00. Tickets will not be sold on site for foreign visitors who do not make a reservation.

Best time to visit: Early morning for peaceful atmosphere and tai chi practice. Evenings ideal for boating as sunset paints the lake. After 8pm, illuminations light up the White Dagoba, Yong'an Bridge, Yilan Hall and Five-Dragon Pavilions.
